title: Enough for now
hookLine: a present judgment, a present act, a present acceptance: that's enough (Meditations 9.6)

lines: A LIST BUILT NOT TO END.
cards: Your phone shows you a hundred things you could want. A better kitchen, a different job, a calmer family, the trip, the body, the version of you that's on top of everything.
The list never ends because it isn't built to end. Then, in book nine, Marcus writes an entry only one sentence long, and in George Long's English it finishes on a word that list never says. Enough.

teach.b: Marcus writes, roughly: your present judgment, grasping things as they are; your present action, done for the common good; your present acceptance of whatever comes from outside you. These are enough. Look at the parts.
A judgment: seeing this moment truly. An action: doing this moment's work for others. An acceptance: being at peace with what this moment brought.
Each one happens now. None of them needs a future that hasn't arrived. That's why enough is radical.
So much of what drives us says not yet: not until the promotion, the cure, the apology.
Marcus says the three things a good life needs are all available in the present, and that's sufficient.
Not perfect. Sufficient. The Greek verb behind that word means it suffices.
And the week, looking back: the spring runs clear, poured out, teach or bear, we're one fabric, nature's work, he's hurt himself, and now, it suffices.
Seven entries, and every one pulls the same way: away from what other people do and what tomorrow might bring, toward what you can see, do and accept right here.
Across books eight and nine, the lesson keeps coming back to the same small size: this moment, and three things you can do in it.

how: Some readers of the Meditations use this entry as a short evening check: did I see truly, act for others, and accept what came today? If so, the day was enough.

o: three gifts you hope to receive this year
true judgment, good action, acceptance, all now
the past, present and future held at once

games.q: enough for now — tap the pairs.
p: peace with what comes from outside

s: Marcus says a good life needs the right future first
he says three present things are enough: judgment, action, acceptance.
the whole entry is a single sentence
it names the three presents and ends: that's enough.

games.q: you're Marcus at the end of a long day. nothing is finished. what do you tell yourself?
o: I'll be content once the war is won.
a true judgment, a good act, an acceptance, now: that's enough.
nothing counts until everything is done.
games.why: he writes that the present judgment, the present action and the present acceptance are enough, without waiting on the future.

practice: Name one thing about this exact moment you've been fighting, the noise, the tiredness, the weather, and without pretending to like it, say inside: this is what's here.
Then check the three: am I seeing this moment truly, is there something good I can do in it, can I accept what it brought? If you can answer, that's enough.

wordCard.voice: Three presents. Marcus's list: a true judgment, an action for the common good, an acceptance of what comes. They suffice. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: it is enough, it suffices. the word for 'enough' in this entry.

carryVoice: Your line: it suffices. Judgment, action, acceptance: not perfect, just sufficient. That's the week, done.
